title: Maryland v. Wilson (1997)
key_points: Holding: Federally, officers may order passengers out of a lawfully stopped car without further justification.
New Jersey: State v. Smith, 134 N.J. 599 (1994) requires specific facts creating a heightened awareness of danger before ordering a passenger out.
officer_notes: Scenario: During a stop you want the front passenger out of the car.
Takeaway: In NJ, apply State v. Smith instead.
